## All rows (source_id order)
- [S0973] types=[PRINCIPLE, DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "States provenance can be falsified: Provenance != AuthenticProvenance. Separates six related-but-distinct concepts: Identity ('who or what is this?' -- proves nothing about truth; experiment 1 rejects inferring p=True merely because an identity is valid and asserted p); Authenticity ('did this artifact actually originate from the claimed identity?', VerifySignature(a,Agent_A)->True/False); Integrity ('has the artifact changed since creation/signing?', a hash H(a) changing to H(a') on modification -- experiment 2 detects IntegrityViolation, and Integrity != Truth, experiment 3 shows a validly-signed false claim gives Authentic=True but TruthStatus=Conflicted, 'cryptography protects provenance and integrity; it does not manufacture truth'); Authority ('is this identity authorized to make this statement/decision?', context-scoped -- experiment 4 rejects an authority overreach from TechnicalAnalysis into FinancialAuthorization); Trust (Trust(x,y,C,t), contextual and non-transferable across domains -- experiment 5 rejects transferring code-analysis reliability into financial-decision authority); and Provenance itself." (anchor: "Provenance != AuthenticProvenance; six concepts requiring separation (Identity/Authenticity/Integrity/Authority/Trust/Provenance)")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Distinguishes empirically-estimable Reliability(A,C) = correct/evaluated outcomes from Trust, which may additionally incorporate authority, security, provenance, policy, and historical behavior -- experiment 6: 99% accuracy with a compromised identity does not automatically give Trust=99%. Introduces asymmetric cryptographic identity (sk,pk), signing sigma=Sign_sk(H(a)), verification Verify_pk(a,sigma); experiment 7 accepts AuthenticOrigin=A given valid verification (subject to key-management assumptions). Notes CryptographicTrust depends on KeyManagement: experiment 8 shows a compromised sk_A producing technically-valid signatures for forged content a', requiring the system to consider key revocation/status. Gives identity a lifecycle (Active/Suspended/Revoked/Expired) and requires IdentityValidityAtTime: experiment 9 confirms a signature made before revocation (SignTime<t_revocation) remains HistoricalSignatureValid subject to the trust model, connecting to temporal epistemics (TruthAtTime and IdentityValidityAtTime both required, so Trust must potentially be time-indexed)." (anchor: "Reliability != Trust; sk/pk signature model with key compromise/revocation and temporal IdentityValidityAtTime")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Constructs a cryptographic provenance chain A0 --Sign--> A1 --Transform--> A2 --Sign--> A3, each transformation recording InputHash, OutputHash, ActorIdentity, TransformationVersion. Experiment 10: A2 claiming derivation from A1 but with a mismatched recorded input hash yields ProvenanceIntegrityViolation -- PASS. Extends this to a graph G=(V,E) with cryptographically-bearing edges (Actor, Timestamp, Transformation, InputHash, OutputHash); experiment 11: an attacker forging DerivedFrom(A3,A2) into DerivedFrom(A3,A9) yields GraphIntegrityViolation given protected provenance records -- PASS. Introduces Merkle-style hash trees (H_root=H(H_1,...,H_n)) for large provenance structures, letting a verifier check membership without storing every verification result independently. States explicitly: the architectural requirement is TamperEvidence, not Blockchain -- 'we do not need blockchain... a cryptographically verifiable append-only event history can be implemented with conventional infrastructure'. Experiment 12: replacing ordinary append-only storage with blockchain solely because 'knowledge must be trustworthy' yields NotRequired -- 'trust properties must be derived from actual requirements'." (anchor: "Cryptographic provenance chain with hash-linked transformations; broken/forged-edge detection; Merkle tamper evidence; no-blockchain-required principle")
- [S0973] types=[PRINCIPLE, DISTINCTION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Restates: Sign_A(p)=Valid tells us only that A authored/signed p, not that p=True -- Authenticity is orthogonal to truth. Experiment 13: a validly signed 'the server is healthy' with no actual server evidence yields AuthenticatedClaim, not VerifiedSystemState -- PASS. Gives a five-layer trust model: Layer 1 Identity (who?), Layer 2 Authenticity (did they produce it?), Layer 3 Integrity (was it modified?), Layer 4 Epistemic validity (does evidence justify the claim?), Layer 5 Authority (are they permitted to perform this operation?). Later reinforces with the principle AuthenticEvidence != ReliableEvidence (someone can honestly and authentically provide bad information) -- experiment 22: internally consistent, cryptographically authentic evidence from a historically unreliable source yields Authentic=True but EvidenceStrength not automatically high -- PASS; and ReliableSource != CorrectEveryTime (statistics remain probabilistic, uncertainty must be preserved)." (anchor: "Authenticity is orthogonal to truth (restated); AuthenticEvidence != ReliableEvidence; four/five-layer trust model")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Defines TrustAssessment(a) = f(Identity, Authenticity, Integrity, Authority, EpistemicSupport, Context, Time) -- 'no single Boolean can represent all of this safely'. Experiment 14: storing a bare trusted=true for an artifact with valid identity/integrity but absent authority and weak evidence is Rejected as an insufficient trust representation -- PASS. Warns against one enormous Trust aggregate, recommending separate concepts (Identity, Credential, Authority, EvidenceAssessment, Provenance) with explicit relationships, potentially separate bounded contexts (IdentityContext, EvidenceContext, KnowledgeContext, GovernanceContext) integrated via contracts. Experiment 15: a universal TrustObject bundling identity/authorization/reliability/truth/evidence/risk/reputation yields GodObjectRisk -- explicitly FAIL." (anchor: "Unified TrustAssessment function rejects a single trusted=true flag; God-Object TrustObject FAILs")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Introduces delegated authority chains (A delegates to B, B may authorize only within its delegated scope); experiment 16: B granting C a scope S1∪S2 it never possessed (only S1) yields DelegationViolation -- PASS. Defines typed Capability=(Subject,Action,Resource,Scope,Validity), stronger than role-only authorization; experiment 17: an agent with Capability(Action=X) attempting Action=Y is Denied -- PASS. Applies the same model to humans: Person != UniversalAuthority (architecture-approval authority does not imply deployment authority) -- experiment 18: role overreach interpreted as deployment authority is Denied -- PASS. Applies it to AI agents with a bounded CapabilitySet (e.g. ReadKnowledge, CreateHypothesis, RunAnalysis, but not AuthorizePayment or DeleteEvidence) -- experiment 19: an unrestricted AI agent receiving full system privileges is a GovernanceFailure -- PASS. States the least-privilege principle Capability(A) subset-of RequiredCapabilities(A), aligning security architecture with DDD responsibility boundaries." (anchor: "Capability-based authorization for humans and AI; delegation-scope violation; least privilege Capability(A)⊆RequiredCapabilities(A)")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "States trust transitivity is not universally valid: Trust(A,B)=High and Trust(B,C)=High does not license Trust(A,C)=High -- experiment 20 rejects that inference -- PASS, 'prevents dangerous trust propagation through agent networks'. Extends the multi-graph family with a Trust graph G_T alongside Knowledge (G_K), Provenance (G_P), Dependency (G_D), and Authority (G_A) graphs, which 'should not be collapsed into one universal graph'. (anchor: "Trust non-transitivity; multi-graph model (G_K,G_P,G_D,G_A,G_T) not collapsible (generic-relation-schema FAILs)")
- [S0973] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Combines Epistemic provenance ('why do we believe this?') with Cryptographic provenance ('can we verify the recorded history?') into VerifiableEpistemicProvenance -- 'a major architectural concept'. (anchor: "VerifiableEpistemicProvenance (cryptographic + epistemic provenance combined); SemanticTrustBoundary between unverified input and trusted state")
